heading: Every simpler form
body:
Each pattern has its own code, so you can search for it. Tachyon suggests each one only where the simpler form does exactly the same thing.

| Code | Pattern | Before | After | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TY1340` | An `if` that only returns true or false | `if (a > b) { return true; } return false;` | `return a > b;` | All languages. In JavaScript, TypeScript, PHP, Python and Ruby only when the condition is a comparison, a `!` or another true-or-false value. |
| `TY1341` | A comparison with true or false | `ready == true`, `ready == false` | `ready`, `!ready` | Java, Go and Rust, where the value is always a boolean. |
| `TY1342` | A choice between true and false | `a > b ? true : false`, `True if a > b else False` | `a > b` | Languages with `? :`, Python, and `if` expressions in Kotlin and Rust. `? false : true` becomes `!(a > b)`. |
| `TY1343` | Keep the matches only to see if there is one | `items.filter(isReady).length > 0` | `items.some(isReady)` | JavaScript and TypeScript (`some`), Java (`anyMatch`), Kotlin (`any`, `none`), C# (`Any`), Ruby (`any?`, `none?`), Dart (`any`), Swift (`contains`). |
| `TY1344` | Find a position only to see if a value is there | `names.indexOf(name) !== -1`, `text.find(word) != -1` | `names.includes(name)`, `word in text` | JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, Kotlin, Dart, Go (`strings.Contains`), PHP (`str_contains`, `in_array`), Python, Ruby (`include?`), Swift. Not C#: its `IndexOf` compares text by culture. |
| `TY1345` | `else` after `return`, `throw`, `break` or `continue` | `if (a) { return 1; } else { b(); }` | `if (a) { return 1; }` then `b();` | All languages. Not when the `else` code declares a name that could clash with another name in the same block. |
| `TY1346` | Two `not` operators | `if (!!user)`, `if not not user:` | `if (user)`, `if user:` | In conditions. In Java, Kotlin, C#, Go, Rust, Swift and Dart everywhere. |
| `TY1347` | A negated equality | `!(a === b)`, `not a == b` | `a !== b`, `a != b` | All languages. Not for `<` and `>`: `!(a < b)` and `a >= b` differ when a value is not a number. |
| `TY1348` | A `return` with no value at the end of a method | `save(); return;` | `save();` | All languages except Ruby (the last value is the result) and Go. |
| `TY1349` | An `if` that holds only another `if` | `if (a) { if (b) { run(); } }` | `if (a && b) { run(); }` | All languages. Not when either `if` has an `else`. |
| `TY1350` | A variable set from its own value | `total = total + price;` | `total += price;` | All languages. In Python and Kotlin only when the variable started as a number or text, so that `+=` cannot change a shared list. |
| `TY1351` | Check for a key, then read it | `cache[key] if key in cache else None` | `cache.get(key, None)` | Python (`get`), Ruby (`fetch`), Java (`getOrDefault`), C# (`GetValueOrDefault`), PHP (`??`). Only when the default is a plain value, so that nothing extra runs. |
| `TY1352` | A loop that only joins or adds up items | `text = ""` then `for part in parts: text += part` | `text = "".join(parts)` | Python and C#, Dart, Swift (join), Kotlin and PHP (join and sum). Not Python or Ruby sums: their `sum` adds decimal numbers more exactly than a loop. |
| `TY1353` | A size compared with zero | `items.length == 0`, `items.size > 0` | `items.empty?`, `items.isNotEmpty()` | Ruby, Kotlin, Java, Dart, Swift and Rust, which have an `empty` method. |
| `TY1354` | An index loop that only reads each item | `for (let i = 0; i < items.length; i++) { const item = items[i]; ... }` | `for (const item of items) { ... }` | All languages except Rust. Only when the loop uses the index for nothing else. |
| `TY1355` | An `if` that only sets true or false | `if (a > b) { big = true; } else { big = false; }` | `big = a > b;` | All languages, with the same rule as TY1340. |

Tachyon does not suggest some forms on purpose. `len(items) == 0` in Python stays as it is, because `not items` asks the reader to know that an empty list counts as false. `if !ready` in Ruby stays as it is, because `unless` is a harder word than `if` and `not`. Reduce and fold chains, nested `? :` choices and comprehensions are never suggested, because they are harder to read than a plain loop.
